properties.name: A collaborator's design work survives clone → write → push → pull without three silent failures on the way
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-13, settling options B and D of `dec:idea-feedback-arrives-by-git-push-and-pull` after asking whether his brother could clone the repo, write feedback straight into the graph, push, and have it arrive on his next pull. **ACCEPTED 2026-08-14 on his word**, after Alex's independent report supplied field evidence for it (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`).

THE ANSWER WAS YES — that path is `dec:multi-writer-architecture`'s intended one, no server, the file is the transport — BUT FOUR STEPS HAVE TO HAPPEN AND THREE FAIL SILENTLY: import before writing (or the fresh store MINTS a new `graph_id`), export before pushing (or `.reflow2/` being ignored means the push carries nothing), a per-clone merge driver (or git line-merges a multi-megabyte JSON graph), and import after pulling.

⇒ **B AND D WERE TAKEN. C WAS NOT, AND THE REASON IS THE REQUIREMENT'S OWN BOUNDARY:** every step here is silent-when-skipped and the instinct is to automate all of them, but step 4 is deliberately manual on `dec:ask-not-repair` — an unasked upsert can overwrite live session work. **Automating an act because forgetting it is expensive is how a tool starts making design decisions on somebody's behalf.** So what is owed is that each step SAYS what it needs, never that it acts unasked.

WHAT THIS REQUIRES, stated so it can be checked:

  B · A project's design record merges per NODE, not by lines. Both halves: the repo-side rule (`.gitattributes`, which travels) and the per-clone driver (`git config`, which cannot — git deliberately refuses to let a repository configure an executable). MEASURED 2026-08-13: `.gitattributes` in reflow2's own repo has carried `merge=reflow2` for months and **`reflow2_init.py` never set the driver**, so any fresh clone fell back to a line merge on a 5 MB graph document, silently.

  D · The shared record having moved reaches a session on an ORDINARY READ, not only when somebody calls `loop_status`. MEASURED: `loop_status` already computed `record_moved` correctly; `read_loop_hint` built its hint from the core `LoopStatus`, which has no sync knowledge, so the one LOUD step of the four was loud only inside a call nobody makes on the way past.

✅ **THE SCOPE OF B, RULED ON 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY AND RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS RAISED AS A WIDENING RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER.** Implementing B, the installer was given a second act nobody had approved: a consumer project with NO `.gitattributes` at all now gets one CREATED, where what he had approved was the per-clone `git config` driver. That was flagged to him at the time and left open; **he has now ruled it IN, on the ground that the two halves are one mechanism** — `git config` says HOW to merge and `.gitattributes` says WHICH files, so a driver without the repo-side rule is inert and the silent line-merge survives untouched. It appends to an existing file and **never replaces one**, the same restraint `write_mcp_config` and `ensure_hooks` already show.
  ⚠️ THE COST HE ACCEPTED, stated plainly: `init` now writes a git configuration file into a repository that did not ask for one. Two narrower readings were on the table and were NOT taken — printing the line for the user to add (rejected: the step is silent-when-skipped, which is the failure class this requirement exists to close), and writing it only for a repo that has a remote (rejected as a refinement, though `dec:install-once-per-machine` — *"the in-repo half is optional and only for repos you share"* — is the argument that would revive it if the file is ever felt to be intrusive).

📌 NEITHER MAY ACT. The hint says the record moved and names `import_graph`; taking it in stays the reader's decision. The installer registers a driver and **leaves alone one somebody else set**.

⚠️ WHAT IS STILL OPEN, AND DELIBERATELY: step 1 (import-on-first-use, option C) and step 2's discoverability beyond what `req:a-consumer-project-ends-up-with-a-committable-record` already fixed. Step 2 is the one Alex actually hit, and it is worth recording that HIS FEEDBACK ROUTE DEPENDED ON A FEATURE THAT DID NOT EXIST UNTIL THE SAME DAY — before that fix his push would have succeeded and carried nothing.

📌 CONFIRMED IN THE FIELD 2026-08-14: Alex's report *"none of them were the graph json file that could be committed to a repo and pulled down and utilized by another project member"* is THREE clauses, and it took two PRs to answer them — #172 made the record committable, #174 made it pullable and usable by a second person. #172 alone would have left him a file he could commit and a broken multi-writer path beneath it. His residual *"I didn't think `.reflow2/` was loaded into a project anymore"* is a mental-model gap now addressed in the ignore rule's own comment (*"machine state, NOT the design"*) and in the install summary: machine-wide INSTALL does not mean machine-wide GRAPH, because `req:persistence` keeps the design in-repo beside the code.
